newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel in W. Bank land confiscation push -lawmaker.
newsitem.headline: Israel in W. Bank land confiscation push -lawmaker.

text.p: Israel has confiscated about 7,500 acres (3,040 hectares) of Palestinian land in the occupied West Bank this year in a drive to expand Jewish settlements, a left-wing Israeli legislator said on Monday.

Dedi Zucker of Israel's opposition Meretz party said on the eve of an Israeli-Egyptian summit that Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai had approved the seizures. Mordechai's office declined immediate comment.

"If land seizure and approval of zoning plans, which will lead to more construction, continues at the current pace, the size of (existing) settlements and their population will grow significantly within a year or two," Zucker said in a report.
Some 130,000 Jews live in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, areas captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war where Palestinians want to establish their own state.
The United States said last week, in a report disputed by Israel, that the Jewish state had no need to expand settlements since a quarter of the homes in them stood empty.
Zucker's report, which his aide said was based on statistics from Israel's Peace Now group and the Palestinian Authority, detailed land confiscations from Arab villages across the West Bank.

The right-wing government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has pledged to widen existing Jewish settlements and started work in March on a project to build 6,500 homes for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem.
Construction of the Har Homa project on a hilltop Palestinians call Jabal Abu Ghneim plunged the Middle East peace process into crisis and halted peace talks with the PLO.
Netanyahu, due to hold a summit on Tuesday with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on reviving Middle East peacemaking, has vowed to continue the East Jerusalem settlement despite Arab opposition.

"The meeting can only succeed if Mr Netanyahu, in good faith and courage, comes to the meeting and does what needs to be done in order to put the peace process back on track -- and that is to...freeze all settlement activities," Palestinian cabinet minister Nabil Shaath told reporters in Gaza.
